lines.speaker: harrow
lines.text: Keep your voice down, friend, and welcome to what's left of Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: harrow
lines.text: Gate's shut after dusk. Keep it low.

lines.speaker: harrow
lines.text: You shout like that again and I'll put you out through the thorn myself.

lines.speaker: lyra
lines.text: You came. Sit, keep your voice in your chest. I've a thing to ask that I should not ask anyone.
lines.when: !(flags.lyra_wg_met || flags.lyra_dw_met)   // from voices.js lyraState(): after Whisper-Grove she is silent until flags.lyra_voice, then speaks as lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra
lines.text: Come in, close the door. The lamp's lit; we can talk.
lines.when: !(flags.lyra_wg_met || flags.lyra_dw_met)   // from voices.js lyraState(): after Whisper-Grove she is silent until flags.lyra_voice, then speaks as lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra
lines.text: Lower. Please. There are things in this town that learn from every sound.
lines.when: !(flags.lyra_wg_met || flags.lyra_dw_met)   // from voices.js lyraState(): after Whisper-Grove she is silent until flags.lyra_voice, then speaks as lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Mind the bed, twenty paces off the door. No sound carries over it for a day. Say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: The hounds let you past. That means you came quietly. Good.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I don't build things anymore. I just know how they break. What do you want broken?

lines.speaker: hetty
lines.text: Sit anywhere that isn't broken. Small beer or smaller. We do not sing in here, not since Davin.

lines.speaker: hetty
lines.text: Beer's a copper. Rooms are a sovereign. Singing is free and it will get you killed.

lines.speaker: hetty
lines.text: I've put bigger men than you out of here for raising their voice. Sit.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Every sailor dies, friend. The trick is to be somewhere else when it happens. Sit; I'm buying, because I'm frightened.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Corsair, Rust Coast, retired from the sea on account of the sea. What'll you have?

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Ha! You have the look of somebody about to tell me something I already know and have been drinking not to hear.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: I have cut more limbs than any butcher in the Reach and done every one with care. Sit. I will not chalk your door today.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: The sap-mark means past cutting. Now it also means the Inquisitor's list. Keep that to yourself.

lines.speaker: rooke
lines.text: Lower your voice in my surgery or I will lower it for you with a needle.

lines.speaker: orla
lines.text: Come closer, I cannot turn. Are you here about Davin?

lines.speaker: orla
lines.text: Mind the roots on the floor. They are mine.

lines.speaker: orla
lines.text: I am a tree with a tongue; shout at me if you like, I cannot leave.

lines.speaker: pim
lines.text: Shh. Mam says I'm not to talk to anybody about my hands.

lines.speaker: pim
lines.text: I'm not supposed to be out. Don't tell.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: Pitch has a colour, through these lenses. Yours is an unremarkable brown. State your business.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: The Consortium pays this town's bread. Remember that before you speak.

lines.speaker: vosk
lines.text: I have Legionnaires. You have a voice. One of those is replaceable.

lines.speaker: aldric
lines.text: The seal of Queen Maelis bids you welcome. Her signature on the decrees is famously steady for a woman dead a hundred and forty years.

lines.speaker: aldric
lines.text: Yes? Be brief. I have the Factor at one shoulder and the Church at the other.

lines.speaker: aldric
lines.text: You sold them, my son says. I fed them, I say. Which of us do you think is lying?

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Night shift. Keep it under the pumps and the bells won't turn. Are you — are you with him? With Engineer Vance?

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Nobody comes down here who isn't on the roster. Which you aren't.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Quiet! The Legionnaire in Depot Three walks when it hears boots.

lines.speaker: bettany
lines.text: Softly, love. What ails? I have tonic, I have honey for the throat, and I have shot, which I do not approve of and sell anyway.

lines.speaker: bettany
lines.text: Tonic's five. Honey's four. Shot's three the three. Keep your voice down while you count.

lines.speaker: bettany
lines.text: I hummed half this town into the world. I will not be barked at in my own stall.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Sit if you like. She comes on the water about this time. You will hear her if you keep still.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Hm. You are standing where I listen.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Lower your voice. She will not come if you shout.

lines.speaker: hob
lines.text: Evening. Mind the vats; the lime does not care who you are.

lines.speaker: hob
lines.text: Tannery's shut. Nobody wants leather off a town that is turning to wood.

lines.speaker: hob
lines.text: I have buried two apprentices this year. Try me.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: He is not to be looked at. Whoever you are. He has a cough.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: The mill is shut. Say what you want through the door next time.

lines.speaker: nell
lines.text: Get out of my mill.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: The Note is held. You may speak under it. Quietly, and in tune.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: This chapel had bells once. The Synod took them for bore-teeth, and it was right to. A bell is a voice with nobody inside it.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: I have burned men for less than that tone. I am tired, and the Note is long, and you will not try me again.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Evening. Keep it low.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Hm?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.text: Lower your voice before something hears you.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.text: Blessings of the Narrow on you. Softly, now.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.text: Yes? Quietly.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.text: Hush! The children.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: a stranger, polite, at the wrong end of the continent. Sit. Not there. That is where the proctors will come from.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I am a list, not a cure. Say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Precision, please. I record everything, including the tone.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Mind the ladder; the third rung is a liar. She'll hold at the mast-height as long as the tanks do, and the tanks are not what they were.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: OK-114, under two coats of paint. She's initialled it eleven times, your scribe. I can tell by the way she looks at my hull.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Say it quick. I don't like a city that doesn't fall down.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Listen. Under the water. Seven forty-one, very faint. The presses.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: This is a dead city that never fell down. That is a statistical anomaly. I do not like anomalies.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: My arm locks when that note is struck near it. Keep me away from the grey men, or keep them away from me.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the stranger is polite in a drowned city. Noted.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I am a list, not a cure.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Precision, please. I record everything, including the tone.

lines.speaker: halder
lines.text: Four plates. The blue one is Bryony's.

lines.speaker: halder
lines.text: The boys will be in directly.
segments: the boys will be in directly

lines.speaker: halder
lines.text: Sit, sit, there's four.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: Hot water? There is always hot water. Sit; the chair is clean. People hesitate less when the chair is clean.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: You are not on my list, which means you are on someone else's. Sit down.

lines.speaker: quist
lines.text: Lower your voice. There are people being registered in the next room, and it upsets them.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.speaker: lamplighter
lines.text: The lamps are late tonight.

lines.speaker: lamplighter
lines.text: The lamps are late tonight.

lines.speaker: lamplighter
lines.text: The lamps are late tonight.

lines.speaker: bettis
lines.text: Name, please.

lines.speaker: bettis
lines.text: Name, please.

lines.speaker: bettis
lines.text: Name, please.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Ten heartbeats. I counted. This time I didn't cut.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: She's on her side in the willows with a hole in her number-three tank you could post a sheep through. We are not leaving by air today.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Don't. I know. I put a tree through an Office cutter. It seemed like the thing to do.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Don't touch that. Or that. That one you can touch, it's already broken.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: Number-three tank. Look at it. I could weep. I nearly have.

lines.speaker: tobiah
lines.text: I'm an engine man in a forest. Say something useful or hold this.

lines.speaker: mags
lines.text: Slower. I read lips, not minds.
lines.delivery: flat, dry; the first word is an instruction, the second sentence a dry aside

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Seven forty-one is gone. I can hear the woods instead. They are very loud.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Not now.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Entry: the Deep Woods. One wreck, eleven souls, a press, and me.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Two things left in the inventory, and the third does not feel like a gap. It feels like a shelf.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: I am counting. Wait.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.

lines.speaker: sexton
lines.text: One more before the light goes. One more.
segments: one more before the light goes

lines.speaker: sexton
lines.text: Deep enough. Not deep enough. One more.

lines.speaker: mourner
lines.text: Lilies for the Cantor. Lilies.

lines.speaker: mourner
lines.text: We're late. The bell hasn't gone.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Hello.
lines.delivery: very loud, a child who forgets to be quiet

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Hello.
lines.delivery: very loud, a child who forgets to be quiet

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Hello.

lines.speaker: weaver
lines.text: {name}, come in now, the water's warm.
segments: come in now, the water's warm
lines.delivery: warm, coaxing, trailing; {name} is the player's FIRST name only (p.name.split(' ')[0]), said twice in the game text ("{name}... {name}, come in now"); function takes the player

lines.speaker: weaver
lines.text: The blue one is Bryony's. The boys will be in directly.
segments: the boys will be in directly

lines.speaker: weaver
lines.delivery: sung: the calling-song, beautifully, in Lyra's voice, the voice she does not have any more; no words in the game text

lines.speaker: weaver
lines.text: I am a list, not a cure.
segments: I am a list, not a cure,
lines.delivery: soft, flat; followed by laughter in eleven children's voices (nonverbal, mix separately)

lines.speaker: weaver
lines.text: Hymn nine, page forty. All rise. All rise.
lines.delivery: two hundred voices, all slightly out of time, trailing

lines.speaker: weaver
lines.text: Seven forty-one. I wrote it down myself.

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: Lark. Lark, come in now, the house is warm.
segments: Lark, come in now, the house is warm.
lines.delivery: warm, fatherly; the first "Lark" is a call, the rest follows

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: Line ninety-four. I initialled it. I was sure for three seconds.
segments: I initialled it. I was sure for three seconds.

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.delivery: sung: the funeral office of Tobin Ashgrove in Tobin Ashgrove's voice, beautifully, a third above Lyra; no words in the game text

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: I can't read, lark. I only know what was said out loud.
segments: I only know what was said out loud.
lines.delivery: gently; the text names no mimicked voice, only that it speaks gently and says "lark"

lines.speaker: requiem
lines.delivery: sung: a funeral office for Marta Hale in a hundred voices, all mourners; no lyric in the game text

lines.speaker: requiem
lines.text: Earth to earth, note to note.
segments: Earth to earth, note to note,
lines.delivery: sung, a Cantor three hundred years dead, solemn

lines.speaker: requiem
lines.delivery: sung: the calling-song in Lyra's own voice as she had it at twelve; no words in the game text

lines.speaker: requiem
lines.text: He was a good man, he was a good man, he was a good man.
segments: he was a good man, he was a good man, he was a good man
lines.delivery: murmured litany, every voice that ever said it here, trailing

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: {name}.
lines.delivery: warm, exact, the way it used to say it when you were in trouble; {name} = the player's full name (G.player.name)
lines.when: trigger hedge_voice; voice is flags.bio_brother ? your brother : flags.bio_coast ? a first mate you once left in the water : someone you buried

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: There's a way through. I can show you. Just say you're there.
segments: There's a way through. I can show you. Just say you're there.
lines.when: trigger hedge_voice (same kin voice as wearer.hedge.0)

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: I'm here.
lines.delivery: warm laugh, then the words in the player's own voice; recorded as a generic voice, cannot clone the player

lines.speaker: wearer
lines.text: Grab the line.

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND. THE. SINGERS.
lines.delivery: slow, three separate struck syllables-words, bronze chord under it

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: DEFEND THE SINGERS.
lines.delivery: loud bronze chord-voice; stencilled on its chest, awake hostile

lines.speaker: aegis
lines.text: Forty-one thousand and five.
lines.delivery: a boy's voice from inside the bronze, small, saying a number; said three times in the game text (repeat x3 with a pause)

lines.speaker: core_voice
lines.text: {name}.
lines.delivery: a small voice from inside the cracked bell or core; said three times in the game text; each enemy carries a name (e.name) from NAMES_POOL or its map placement
lines.when: enemy def.core && e.name; applies to legionnaire, proctor, marine, bosun, outrider, captain (and hushwarden)

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: SHE IS GIVEN. THE QUIET IS MERCIFUL. GO.
segments: SHE IS GIVEN. THE QUIET IS MERCIFUL. GO.
lines.delivery: SIGNED in hand-cant in the game (his mouth is bound with linen). If voiced at all: a low murmur through linen. Safe to omit.
lines.when: flags.mags_cant (shown only if the player can read hand-cant)

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: WHO TAUGHT YOU.
lines.delivery: SIGNED in hand-cant in the game (his mouth is bound with linen). If voiced at all: a low murmur through linen. Safe to omit.
lines.when: after the player signs "The Hush is quiet. It is not merciful." (wildsPeace)

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: THEN SHE IS YOURS TO KEEP LOUD,
segments: THEN SHE IS YOURS TO KEEP LOUD,
lines.delivery: SIGNED in hand-cant in the game (his mouth is bound with linen). If voiced at all: a low murmur through linen. Safe to omit.
lines.when: after the player signs "A woman who stopped hearing." (wildsPeace)

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: About time. I go where it's loudest and break what's about to break. You keep us in the Narrow.
lines.delivery: dry; the first words a wry greeting; a faint glass ring may sit under them
segments: I go where it's loudest and break what's about to break. You keep us in the Narrow.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Hear that? The tombs are holding a chord under the floor. Something in here is about to break, and it isn't the stone.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Old bronze. Cracked at the lip, on the east side. Ring it hard and it'll go the rest of the way.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Quiet. Glass won't ring inside one. Iron, and keep moving.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: A funeral office with nobody in it. My arm hates it.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Marble. Hit it where it's already cracked: the elbows.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Office. They hear better than they fight. Kill the horn first.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Static on legs. Cut the threads, not the spider.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: That one's full. I can hear them in her, waiting to hatch.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: They're not making a sound. Not breathing, not footfalls. That takes practice.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Crossbows. Close the distance, or get a willow between you and them.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Felted bell. Don't let it touch you before you've sung what you need.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Hounds. They won't touch the glass. Stay near me.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: You're bleeding into the moss. Back off and let me take it.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Wake me if the arm starts ringing. You'll hear it before I do.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I'm fine. The arm's ringing, that's all. Give me a minute.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I don't build things anymore. I just know how they break.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Every willow here has a split about a hand above the root. Damp gets in. Give it ten years.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: The glass is louder out here. Like standing next to a bore that's still turning.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: My father sold the Root to keep the town fed. I keep trying to hate him for it. I keep doing the arithmetic instead.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Lyra taught me the Root note when we were nine. I still hum it when the arm's bad. Don't tell her.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Hounds won't come near the glass. Neither will most people. It's restful.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: There. That's what it sounds like when something stops.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Structural failure. Finally.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Next.
lines.delivery: flat; follows the narration that he flexes the glass hand until it stops ringing

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Not yet. Rest first. Then ask me again.
lines.when: flags.part4 && G.party.downed.kaelen (camp, after he went down)
segments: Rest first. Then ask me again.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Suits me.
lines.source: party.js camp dialogue ("Stay by the fire.")

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Quiets. Iron, not glass. Get between them and her.
lines.when: Kaelen is the active companion, order != wait, same map; hush-gift event

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Five of them. I can hear the sickles. Say the word.
lines.when: Kaelen is the active companion, order != wait, same map; Deacon event

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I'll hum. Under the breath, the way the night-hummers do at the crossings. The Hush won't get near you while I'm humming. I can't do anything about the hounds.
segments: Under the breath, the way the night-hummers do at the crossings. The Hush won't get near you while I'm humming. I can't do anything about the hounds.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: The House of the Veil. The scribes kept everyone's names in here. I never thought I'd walk on theirs.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Nobody has rung for the dead out here in three years. You can hear it in the woods. They're waiting.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: That's the office for the dead, sung wrong. Every third line missing. It makes my teeth ache.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I can't sing near it. Nothing can. Don't let it get between us.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: They cut out their own tongues to be holy. I taught children whose parents did that.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: They're wearing voices. Little ones. Don't listen too closely.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Hounds. Stay low. I'll keep us in the Narrow.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: It's listening for me. It has been listening for me since Oakhaven.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Chord-Wardens. They guard the Cantors. Nobody told them there's no one left to guard.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Grey coats. Keep me behind you.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Hold still. I've got you.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I'll take first watch. I'll hum. Sleep.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I'm not built for this. I'm a teacher.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I told my father once that a martyr is just a musician who gave up before the coda. He wrote it down.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Feet on the moss, not the twigs. Breathe through your nose. There. That's the Narrow. You're good at it.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I remember the name of everyone I have sung into the ground. It's the only thing I'm vain about.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Kaelen hums when the arm is bad. He thinks I don't know. I'm the one who taught him that note.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: The reed orchards used to sing in a west wind. Whole hillsides of them. You would have liked it.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Don't thank me for the healing. Thank me when we're all home.
lines.delivery: low, warm; her own ruined voice

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Rest now. Whoever you were.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: It's over. Breathe. It's over.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Not yet. Let me sit a while. Rest, and ask me again.
segments: Let me sit a while. Rest, and ask me again.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: I'll keep it warm.
lines.source: party.js camp dialogue ("Stay by the fire.")

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Put out that lamp. Quiets go to the light. Put it out.
lines.delivery: urgent, low, a sound she has never made before it
lines.when: flags.lyra_voice && Lyra is the active companion, order != wait, same map; hush-gift event
segments: Quiets go to the light. Put it out.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: He thinks he is being kind. That is the worst of it.
lines.when: flags.lyra_voice && Lyra is the active companion, order != wait, same map; Deacon event

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Tell him the Cantor says we heard the question too.
lines.delivery: steady, her own ruined voice, formal

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is autumn, in the four hundred and nineteenth year of the Synod Reckoning. Seven years ago the Light let go.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You have come up the Greenroot road to Oakhaven, capital of the Resonant Reach, a town that lives inside a hedge three men deep of thorn and packed wool, planted to swallow its own sounds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Too loud brings the hounds. Too still brings the Hush. Every child here can skip to the rhyme.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Church is coming up the road behind you, singing under glass-fire. In nine days it will hold its Pure Note over this town, and a Cantor will be walked down a shaft in white to sing a god to sleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody has rung a bell in Oakhaven since the Synod took them all for bore-teeth. Tonight is Nullday, the old rest-day, the day people fear.

lines.speaker: ignatius
lines.text: One note. One law. One hand.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: By the Arbiterium of the Iron Synod, under the hand of the Supreme Arbiter, at the Organum, the seventeenth day of Leaffall, 419.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: Be it known: the persons styled Kaelen Vance, late Chief Resonant Engineer, badge four-oh-eight-A; Lyra Ashgrove, Cantor, of Oakhaven; the carrier styled Vane, of registry OK-114; and the scribe styled Sable, formerly of the Office of the Catalogue, are declared Dissonant.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: Their goods are forfeit. Their testimony is void in any court of the Synod. The Church of the Pure Note has entered a claim upon the Cantor, which claim the Arbiterium has stayed, for now.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: Be it further known that the Justiciar Aurelian Vaelen, Dread Arbiter, is upon the Iron Tramway with a column of the Carillon Legions and the authority of the Scales, and will be at the Mausoleum of Chords within nine days.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: And be it known that grace is offered, once.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: To Kaelen Vance: surrender of his person at the Organum, upon these terms. The glass shall be drawn. The Supreme Arbiter attests, upon his own body, that it can be drawn, and that he has carried eighty years of it and will show the engineer how.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: To the Cantor Lyra Ashgrove: amnesty, full and recorded, and the Church's claim extinguished, and transit to any province she names.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: To the persons of Oakhaven aboard the said vessel: relief, transit, and registration waived.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Waived. He knows what we saw at the Malting.

lines.speaker: herald
lines.text: And to the consignment of engram cores presently aboard the said vessel: proper disposition by the Office of the Catalogue, under the Registrar-General's hand.

lines.speaker: vane

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Now you're going to walk into the Organum and lie down on a table for the man who used you, and every single time, Kaelen, every single time, the plan is only Kaelen goes into the dark.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: It's twenty-one people off this ship and out of a war.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: It's four hundred and thirty-two people into a furnace! Proper disposition. You heard it. Say what it means.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.speaker: tideweaver

lines.speaker: tideweaver
lines.text: This did not happen. It also did not unhappen; nothing does.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: I'd like to put one thing in.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: I've been thinking about it since the herald started, which is longer than I usually think about anything. Nine days, he said. That's a column on the Tramway with a Justiciar at the head of it, and they'll be at this clearing on Driftday, and the Kestrel can't fly on three tanks.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: vane
lines.text: Which means the choice isn't Kaelen goes in or nobody goes in. It's Kaelen goes in and buys us nine days we'd have had anyway, because that writ already told us where they are and how fast. It's a bad trade, that's all I'm saying. I've made a career of bad trades and that one's bad.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: He also told us something else.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: Think about the terms. Amnesty for the Cantor, transit for twenty-one farmers, registration waived.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: The Registrar-General would never waive registration; it is the only thing he has. And the cores returned, which the Catalogue would demand anyway. All of that is small.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: And the thing he is buying with it is one man with a Dawning-glass arm who can hear the Choristers.

lines.speaker: kaelen
lines.text: Sable.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: He does not want you punished, Engineer. He wants you at the Organum.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: He has eight Anchors to ask a question of, and a Planetary Engine thirty years in the building, and exactly two people alive who have heard a god answer. He is one of them.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: He is a hundred and forty years old and eighty percent glass and he will not last another twenty years, and he has just offered you a cure, a desk, and an education.

lines.speaker: sable
lines.text: That is not a sentence. That is a succession.

lines.speaker: kaelen

lines.speaker: sable

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: Last night I killed the last place my father's voice existed, and the day before that a thing in a fog told me what you did, kindly, and let me sit down, and both of those are in me now and they are not coming out.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: But I have watched you try to pay for seven years, and the arithmetic is wrong, and I'm the only person here who can say so, because everybody else on this ship wants something from you.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: You can't pay. There isn't enough of you. Eleven thousand and forty people and a sky.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: There is no amount of Kaelen Vance that buys that back, and you have been trying to settle it one limb at a time since the year it happened, and the Supreme Arbiter has just offered you the biggest instalment yet and you lit up like a lamp.

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined
lines.text: So: no. You don't get to pay. You get to help. You get to get up tomorrow and do the next useful thing and then the one after that, for as long as it takes,

lines.speaker: lyra_ruined

lines.text: The General says, state your ship and your business, and say it aloud, and go on saying something after.

lines.speaker: p100_94
lines.text: The General is waiting for you to say that again, in another way.

lines.speaker: p100_94
lines.text: The General says, the Watch holds the wall. The General says, the Watch holds the wall and nothing else.

lines.speaker: p100_94
lines.text: The General says the Watch obeys the Synod when the Synod is not mad. The General says the Synod has been mad since the spring of 413.

lines.speaker: p100_94
lines.text: The General says nothing about that. Spring of 413. The batteries were new and nobody knew how to lay them. She laid them by voice, tower to tower in the dark, for thirty-one hours. At dawn on the second day she opened her mouth to say cease firing, and nothing came out.

lines.speaker: p100_94
lines.text: The General says, keep talking. On the wall, in the yards, on the stairs. The General says, if you go quiet somebody will ring a bell, and they will not look first.

lines.speaker: p100_watcher
lines.text: and then your sister wrote, and the calf was a heifer after all— I can do both. Go on.

lines.speaker: p100_watcher
lines.text: in, and out, that's it, and the calf

lines.speaker: p100_watcher
lines.text: Wake him and you take the next two hours.

lines.speaker: p100_watcher
lines.text: You talk to their breathing. In, and out. If it changes, you talk closer. It has never failed yet in this hall, and nobody wants to be the one it fails for.

lines.speaker: p11_dicer
lines.text: Hetty's board says no dice, and Hetty's board is upstairs. A throw of bones, if you have a coin to lose?

lines.speaker: p11_dicer
lines.text: Bones? One to twenty sovereigns. Nobody down here ever got rich, and nobody has had to leave.

lines.speaker: p11_dicer
lines.text: Bones, or back up the stair,

lines.speaker: p11c_fish
lines.text: Flume eel, the green sort. Do not worry about the colour. It is only the water.

lines.speaker: p11c_fish
lines.text: Eel or nothing.

lines.speaker: p11c_fish
lines.text: You smell of the Hedge. Buy an eel and I will forget.

lines.speaker: p11c_herb
lines.text: Willow-bark, reed-pith, moss. Cut this morning, so it still remembers being green.

lines.speaker: p11c_herb
lines.text: Herbs. Bandage-stuff, if you bleed.

lines.speaker: p11c_herb
lines.text: Handle it or buy it. It bruises.

lines.speaker: p11c_larder
lines.text: Eat something. You have the look of someone who has been listening too hard.

lines.speaker: p11c_larder
lines.text: Honey, eel, tonic. Eat first, ask after.

lines.speaker: p11c_larder
lines.text: Buy or stop breathing on the pies.

lines.speaker: p11c_odds
lines.text: A little of everything, and the everything is mostly quiet.

lines.speaker: p11c_odds
lines.text: Reeds, bottles, pebbles. Do not ask what the pebbles are for.

lines.speaker: p11c_odds
lines.text: Look, do not breathe on it.

lines.speaker: p11c_tinker
lines.text: Mending, selling, sharpening. Mostly selling.

lines.speaker: p11c_tinker
lines.text: Edges and shot. Do not ask where the shot came from.

lines.speaker: p11c_tinker
lines.text: If it is loud, I do not stock it.

lines.speaker: p12_baker
lines.text: Softly, love. New flour, the first in a year that tastes of nearly what it should. Bread, cider, curd. Eat it while it is warm.

lines.speaker: p12_baker
lines.text: Hearth bread, cider, moot-curd. Last Sheaf week. Market prices; I am not here to get rich.

lines.speaker: p12_baker
lines.text: If you are going to shout, buy something first, and shout into the bread.

lines.speaker: p12_baker
lines.text: We bake for the Last Sheaf every year the field is cut. This year the dough is rising and nobody has told the Church.

lines.speaker: p12_baker
lines.text: Flour does not mind the Hedge. Flour minds the damp.

lines.text: Not here. Not now. Ask Harrow.

lines.speaker: p12_dunna
lines.text: Not now. Ask Harrow.

lines.speaker: p12_dunna
lines.text: Hush. Ask Harrow, and ask him quietly.

lines.speaker: p12_herald
lines.text: Blessings of the Pure Note, citizen. Take a place in the square. There is bread after. There is always bread after.

lines.speaker: p12_herald
lines.text: The Rite is a festival. Festivals are attended.

lines.speaker: p12_herald
lines.text: Lower your voice. This is a feast, and feasts are quiet.

lines.speaker: p12_herald
lines.text: A feast for the whole district. Attendance is a courtesy and will be noted.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: Softly, if you would. I stand out here because I cannot sit in there.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: Does it ring? Not next door, it does not. Keep your voice down.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: If you mean to shout, shout at your own door.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: Gil cut reeds. Maud kept the carders' books. Linnet is eight and counts everything she walks past. Nan was Gil's mother, and the oldest voice in this lane. They went out on the last cart before the gate was barred.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: Tuned to you before you can lift your head, and hung over the door. Every reed in this lane stirs a little when the wind comes through the Hedge. The Tarrows' hang still. The wind goes round them.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: It keeps every sound this town ever made. It has your first cry and your mother's last word, and it gives them back when it likes, in whatever voice it was given. That is the only mercy in it.

lines.speaker: p13h_wenna
lines.text: When one of us is dying the family holds their pitch until the body lets go, and counts it out in eights, one for each Anchor. On the eighth, the note is let go. We do it in silence now. It is not that we are afraid. It is that it does not carry.

lines.speaker: p15_dealer

lines.speaker: p15_dealer
lines.text: Rounds, or the next seat,

lines.speaker: p15l_clerk
lines.text: Letters of credit. Gold in, paper out. Do not unfold one near the lamp.

lines.speaker: p15l_clerk
lines.text: If you want to shout, shout at the Factor. If you want a letter, speak low.

lines.text: You are welcome at the desk. It is not much of a desk. Everything on it is kept.

lines.speaker: p15l_veil

lines.speaker: p15s_preacher
lines.text: Peace, under the Note. Sit, if there is a place. We begin when the last of us has stopped talking.

lines.speaker: p15s_preacher
lines.text: The Note is held. There is a place at the end of the bench, if you want it.

lines.speaker: p15s_preacher
lines.text: Lower your voice. This is a listening, and you are in the middle of it.

lines.speaker: p15s_preacher
lines.text: We are not here to frighten anyone. A frightened town sings out of tune, and a held town sings one note, and the quiet has nothing to take.

lines.speaker: p15s_preacher
lines.text: Hearthday. Attendance is a courtesy. I would come. It will be a long note.

lines.speaker: p16f_hand

lines.speaker: p16f_madge
lines.text: Put it on the board or put it back.

lines.speaker: p16f_orrin
lines.text: If you are not here about the wheel, you are in the way of the wheel.

lines.speaker: p16f_pellam
lines.text: Quietly. The basin carries.

lines.speaker: p16f_wife
lines.text: We are out of tea, patience and luck, in that order.

lines.speaker: p16f_wife
lines.text: Mind your feet near the edge.

lines.speaker: p16h_dessa

lines.speaker: p16k_hob
lines.text: I have buried two apprentices this year. Try me.

lines.speaker: p16k_hob

lines.speaker: p16k_mags

lines.speaker: p16k_nell

lines.speaker: p16k_pennick
lines.text: It is going to fail. I am only deciding which morning.

lines.speaker: p16k_pennick
lines.text: Touch nothing. If you must touch something, tell me what, so I know where to start.

lines.speaker: p16k_pennick

lines.speaker: p16k_pennick

lines.speaker: p16k_vane

lines.speaker: p16k_vane
lines.text: Say it quick. The rail is loose and so is my patience.

lines.speaker: p16k_vane
lines.text: Wood, silk, three tanks and a debt. Pennick would give you a longer list and a worse mood. The repair list is in the hold, nailed to a stanchion. I did not write the prices; the chandlers did.

lines.text: I have a file at the Office that says reliable, does not ask questions. I would like it burned, and I would like to read it first.

lines.text: I brought the oil. Six lamps, and a flask each, he says. I said that is not much of a plan. Take it from the niche by the east lamp.

lines.speaker: p17n_jory
lines.text: Lamps first. The moths come for the light and the dark comes for the rest.

lines.speaker: p17n_jory
lines.text: Mind the lamps.

lines.speaker: p17n_marl
lines.text: Does it ring? Don't answer. There is no breath to spare. Hold the middle of the note and it will find you.

lines.speaker: p17n_marl
lines.text: Low and slow. That is all the old ones ever asked.

lines.speaker: p17n_marl
lines.text: Sing, or sit down.

lines.speaker: p17n_tansy
lines.text: Is it always this cold? Marl says it is the coldest place in the Reach. I thought he was being a Cantor about it.

lines.speaker: p17n_tansy
lines.text: I keep losing my place on the turn.

lines.speaker: p17n_tansy
lines.text: I am singing. Look at the lamps.

lines.speaker: p22_absalom
lines.text: Sit down, sit down. My knees have been asking after company.

lines.speaker: p22_absalom
lines.text: Three fires on three hills. I lit them forty back-ends running. Then the Hedge.

lines.speaker: p22_absalom
lines.text: Talk louder. No. Do not. Talk the way you were.

lines.speaker: p22_absalom
lines.text: Long Down to the north, over the Downs; Hob's Knap east, above the orchard; Ewe Barrow west, on the old mound. You can see all three from the Knap, if your eyes are better than mine.

lines.speaker: p22_gideon
lines.text: Sit where the light is. The fire is mutton-fat and it smokes, but it is warm.

lines.speaker: p22_gideon
lines.text: Rooms are a sovereign. Supper is whatever Tamar can spare, and she can spare more than she lets on.

lines.speaker: p22_gideon
lines.text: I opened an inn on a road nobody walks. Say something I have not already said to myself.

lines.speaker: p22_gideon
lines.text: The Bellwether was the drovers' house. Eight hundred sheep a fair-day went past that door. I had it from my uncle and shut it with my own hands the night the Hedge closed, and I opened it again the week Tamar came back up.

lines.speaker: p22_kit
lines.text: Mam says I'm to watch the fold and not the hill. I watch the hill.

lines.speaker: p22_kit
lines.text: Have you seen the Ram? You can't, he's gone green.

lines.speaker: p22_kit
lines.text: I'm not scared of hounds. I'm not.

lines.speaker: p22_kitlost
lines.text: You came. It was making a noise like a lamb. Like a lamb that needed me. And then it was big. It's still in there. Is it still in there?

lines.speaker: p22_tamar
lines.text: Mind the gate, love. It is the only thing between them and the whole of the Reach.

lines.speaker: p22_tamar
lines.text: Farrant. We had the sheep-walk off the Downs for six generations. I am the seventh, and I am starting again.

lines.speaker: p22_tamar
lines.text: If you have come to tell me the hill is not safe, I know. The sheep do not.

lines.speaker: p22_tamar
lines.text: Every sheep in the Reach went into the Hedge. They sheared them for the wool the town packed into the roots, and they drove the Downs flocks in behind the thorn after. Two years shut in. We ate them. Ours too. I fed my children my father's ewes, one a month, and I would do it again. Nothing took them. We did.

lines.speaker: p22_tamar
lines.text: Wethercombe was the sheep-walk's door: the fold, the fair, the Bellwether for the drovers. When the Hedge went up we all went in. I am the first back. Gideon came after me, because somebody has to feed me.

lines.speaker: p29_abel
lines.text: Read the sign? Sheep-walk. There are no sheep. The turf is short anyway, as if it remembers them. I cut it for the Bellwether's fire.

lines.speaker: p29_abel
lines.text: There are no sheep. Nobody says where they went, and I have stopped asking. The combe is down past the stile, if you want people.

lines.speaker: p29_abel
lines.text: There are no sheep. That is what you came to ask, so there it is.

lines.speaker: p29_agnes
lines.text: Mind the flour. I would offer you a chair but they are all full of bread.

lines.speaker: p29_agnes
lines.text: Loaves are two, the honey four. I have not slept since the Hedge went up, so do not haggle; I will cry.

lines.speaker: p29_agnes
lines.text: If you want bread, buy bread. If you want to watch me, the shutters are free.

lines.speaker: p29_ambrose
lines.text: Candles, oil, reeds for the hush-lamps. If it keeps a light lit or a street humming, I have it.

lines.speaker: p29_ambrose
lines.text: Tallow's cheaper. Wax is for the chapel and people who want to be seen buying wax.

lines.speaker: p29_ambrose
lines.text: Buy something or let my door shut. Every draught costs me a candle.

lines.speaker: p29_corvin
lines.text: Timber goes down to Fortis, broadsheets come up from Cantabile, and some of what is in the barrels is neither.

lines.speaker: p29_corvin
lines.text: Tobit sells news; I sell what the news is about.

lines.speaker: p29_corvin
lines.text: Not here. Not loud. Barrels have ears.

lines.speaker: p29_ennis
lines.text: Softly by the skeps, if you would. They take a voice to heart.

lines.speaker: p29_ennis
lines.text: Honey's four. The bees do the work; I only tell them things.

lines.speaker: p29_ennis
lines.text: Not so loud. You will put them off their comb.

lines.speaker: p29_gil
lines.text: Roof to roof, a penny a pole. I know where the street still has a bottom.

lines.speaker: p29_gil
lines.text: Mind the sinkholes. Where the water goes dark, the street went down with it.

lines.speaker: p29_gil
lines.text: Pay or wade.

lines.speaker: p29_hurst
lines.text: Come in off the combe. They are all up at the fold; I mind the soup. There are no sheep, mind. You will have noticed.

lines.speaker: p29_hurst
lines.text: There are no sheep. There were, and now there are none, and the turf keeps the shape of them. That is all I know and all I am saying.

lines.speaker: p29_hurst
lines.text: No, there are no sheep. Everybody asks. Shut the door.

lines.speaker: p29_jem
lines.text: I barred it from the inside because of the woolwight. You came in anyway, so you are either very quiet or not what I thought you were.

lines.speaker: p29_jem
lines.text: Two years of clip and nobody to buy it. I shear what Tamar brings me and I stack it, and I wait for the road to come back.

lines.speaker: p29_jem
lines.text: Bar the door behind you. Properly. Both pins.

lines.speaker: p29_moll
lines.text: That door goes through to the Hollow. Rooke keeps it shut. We hear them in there at night, humming.

lines.speaker: p29_moll
lines.text: Eighty-four in the Hollow, Rooke says, and more since. We send the scraps through for their fires.

lines.speaker: p29_moll
lines.text: No, you cannot go through. Ask Rooke.

lines.speaker: p29_prue
lines.text: Cantabile sheets, three weeks old, still true. The board is free to read; I only charge for the ones I read aloud.

lines.speaker: p29_prue
lines.text: SYNOD REASSURES, it says, every week. I put it up anyway. People like to see what they are not to believe.

lines.speaker: p29_prue
lines.text: Read the board. That is what it is for.

lines.speaker: p29_sexton
lines.text: Salt for the paths, before the town is up. What is buried stays buried, and says nothing.

lines.speaker: p29_sexton
lines.text: Mind the drifts. It is not for the hounds; it is for the ones under the turf.

lines.speaker: p29_sexton
lines.text: Out of the barrow's road.

lines.speaker: p29_sim
lines.text: Abner is outside. He likes the air. I like the work; it stops you hearing the Hollow through the wall.

lines.speaker: p29_sim
lines.text: Lime, then the beam, then the vats. Same as always. The hides are thinner this year, and nobody will say why.

lines.speaker: p29_sim
lines.text: Mind the vats. They do not care whose hand goes in.

lines.speaker: p29_ysolde
lines.text: Salvage, dry and wet. I ask no questions about what you bring me, and you ask none about where I got it.

lines.speaker: p29_ysolde
lines.text: Smugglers' town, they call the Landing. The Rings are where the smuggled things go to wait.

lines.speaker: p29_ysolde
lines.text: Buying or selling? Talking is extra.

lines.speaker: p30_hob
lines.text: Mind the step. I would get up, only it is a business, getting up, on these.

lines.speaker: p30_hob
lines.text: Field-hand. Was. You cannot follow a plough on roots.

lines.speaker: p30_hob
lines.text: Keep 'em dry, she says. I keep 'em dry.

lines.speaker: p30_lissa
lines.text: You can sit on the step if you like. Not on the door. The door is for the house.

lines.speaker: p30_lissa
lines.text: I am not sick. It is only in my arms, Rooke says, up to here. He looks every month.

lines.speaker: p30_lissa
lines.text: Mind my cup.

lines.speaker: p31_jugs
lines.text: ...the blue one, and the white one... the blue one, and the white one...

lines.speaker: p31_shutters
lines.text: ...latched... latched... you can never be too sure...
